source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: said to Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "spoke ... saying" is the usual way of introducing the LORD's words to Moses. Balanced and Readable say it once; Literal keeps both verbs.

source.text: צַ֚ו אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וִֽישַׁלְּחוּ֙ מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה כָּל־צָר֖וּעַ וְכָל־זָ֑ב וְכֹ֖ל טָמֵ֥א לָנָֽפֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Command [the] sons of Israel, and they shall send away from the camp every [one] stricken with scale disease, and every [one] having a discharge, and every [one] unclean by a [dead] person.

en.L: "Command the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel that they send out of the camp everyone with scale disease, and everyone with a discharge, and everyone unclean through a dead person.
en.B: "Command the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to send out of the camp anyone who has a serious skin disease or a discharge, and anyone made unclean by a dead body.
en.R: "Command the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to send certain people out of the camp. This means anyone with a serious skin disease, anyone with a discharge from the body, and anyone who is unclean because of a dead body.

decisions.choice: stricken with scale disease: one of a range of skin conditions that made a person unclean
decisions.reason: The word covers the skin conditions described in Leviticus 13-14, marked by sores, scales or patches, and it is also used of mold on cloth and walls (Leviticus 13:47; 14:34). It is not the same as the disease now called leprosy (Hansen's disease). Leviticus 13:46 already tells such a person to live outside the camp.

decisions.choice: having a discharge: an abnormal flow from the genitals
decisions.reason: Leviticus 15 deals with discharges from the body that made a man or a woman unclean for a time and had to be cleansed with washing and offerings (Leviticus 15:2-15, 25-30).

decisions.choice: unclean by a person: unclean through contact with a dead body
decisions.reason: The word usually means a living person or life, but in this phrase it means a dead person (Leviticus 21:1; Numbers 6:6; 9:6). Numbers 19:11-16 explains that touching a body, or being in the tent where someone has died, makes a person unclean for seven days.

decisions.choice: the camp: the place where the LORD lives among his people
decisions.reason: The three kinds of uncleanness are sent outside the camp because the LORD dwells in it (verse 3). The camp had just been ordered around the tabernacle (chapters 2-4), and what was unclean could not stay near the holy place (Leviticus 15:31).

decisions.choice: a serious skin disease
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the narrower "scale disease". Balanced and Readable use "serious skin disease", as Leviticus 13 does, and avoid "leprosy", which names a different disease today.

source.text: מִזָּכָ֤ר עַד־נְקֵבָה֙ תְּשַׁלֵּ֔חוּ אֶל־מִח֥וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה תְּשַׁלְּח֑וּם וְלֹ֤א יְטַמְּאוּ֙ אֶת־מַ֣חֲנֵיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י שֹׁכֵ֥ן בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: From male to female you shall send away; to outside of the camp you shall send them away, and not they shall defile their camps, which I [am] dwelling in their midst.

en.L: From male to female you shall send [them] away; outside the camp you shall send them, and they shall not defile their camps, where I dwell in their midst."
en.B: Whether male or female, you must send them out and put them outside the camp. Then they will not defile the camps of the people in whose midst I dwell."
en.R: Send away both men and women. Make them stay outside the camp. Then they will not make the camp unclean, because I live there among them."

decisions.choice: from male to female: men and women alike
decisions.reason: Naming the two ends of a range means everyone in between. No one with these kinds of uncleanness was exempt, man or woman.

decisions.choice: their camps: the camp of all Israel, made up of the camps of the tribes
decisions.reason: The plural looks at the camp as the separate camps of the tribes arranged around the tabernacle in chapter 2. All of them together form the one camp of verse 2.

decisions.choice: I dwell in their midst: the LORD lives among Israel
decisions.reason: The verb is the root of the word for the tabernacle, God's "dwelling" (Exodus 25:8-9; 29:45-46). Because the holy God lives in the camp, uncleanness there is not only a private matter; it defiles the place he lives (Leviticus 15:31; Numbers 19:13).

decisions.choice: make the camp unclean
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "defile". Readable uses the plainer "make unclean" and the singular "camp", since the separate tribal camps form one camp.

source.text: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְשַׁלְּח֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם אֶל־מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֵּ֥ן עָשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And did so [the] sons of Israel, and sent them to outside of the camp; just as spoke Yahweh to Moses, so did [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did so, and sent them outside the camp; just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to Moses, so the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did so; they sent them outside the camp. As {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses, so the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did this. They sent those people outside the camp. They did just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses.

decisions.choice: did so ... so did: Israel obeyed exactly
decisions.reason: The verse begins and ends by saying that Israel did as it was told, a pattern that runs through these chapters (Numbers 1:54; 2:34). The repetition stresses complete obedience.

decisions.choice: those people
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are, the unclean people of verse 2, and says the obedience once.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: said to Moses
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

source.text: דַּבֵּר֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ אִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־אִשָּׁ֗ה כִּ֤י יַעֲשׂוּ֙ מִכָּל־חַטֹּ֣את הָֽאָדָ֔ם לִמְעֹ֥ל מַ֖עַל בַּיהוָ֑ה וְאָֽשְׁמָ֖ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel: a man or a woman, when they do any of [the] sins of humankind, by acting unfaithfully [an] unfaithfulness against Yahweh, and is guilty that person,

en.L: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel: 'A man or a woman, when they commit any of the sins of humankind, acting unfaithfully against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and that person is guilty,
en.B: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'When a man or a woman does any wrong to another person, thereby breaking faith with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and that person is guilty,
en.R: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'A man or a woman may do wrong to another person. That is being unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and that person is guilty.

decisions.choice: the sins of humankind: wrongs that people do to one another
alternatives: any of the sins that people commit
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean the sins that human beings commit, or sins committed against a fellow human. What follows points to the second: the guilty person must repay the one who was wronged (verse 7). The law restates Leviticus 5:20-26, where a person cheats or robs a neighbor and so acts unfaithfully against the LORD.

decisions.choice: acting unfaithfully: breaking faith, a breach of trust
decisions.reason: The verb and noun describe disloyalty, taking what is not one's own or betraying a trust (Leviticus 5:15; Joshua 7:1). Wronging a neighbor is counted as unfaithfulness toward the LORD himself, who is witness to the dealings of his people. The same word describes a wife's unfaithfulness in verse 12.

decisions.choice: is guilty: has incurred guilt and must make it right
decisions.reason: The verb means to be guilty or to bear the obligation that guilt brings. It may also include the person's becoming aware of the guilt, which then leads to the confession of verse 7 (Leviticus 5:23).

decisions.choice: wrong(s) another person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the sins of humankind" means here, following the meaning decision. Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

source.text: וְהִתְוַדּ֗וּ אֶֽת־חַטָּאתָם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂוּ֒ וְהֵשִׁ֤יב אֶת־אֲשָׁמוֹ֙ בְּרֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַחֲמִישִׁת֖וֹ יֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֑יו וְנָתַ֕ן לַאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָשַׁ֥ם לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: and they shall confess their sin which they did, and he shall return his guilt [payment] in its head, and its fifth he shall add to it, and give [it] to [the one] whom he was guilty to him.

en.L: then they shall confess their sin that they have committed, and he shall repay his guilt [payment] in full, and add its fifth to it, and give [it] to the one against whom he was guilty.
en.B: they must confess their sin openly. The guilty person must pay back the full amount owed for the wrong, add a fifth to it, and hand it over to the one who was harmed.
en.R: They must admit the sin they have done. They must pay back in full what they owe for the wrong, and add one fifth more. Then they must give it to the person they wronged.

decisions.choice: they confess ... he repays: the same guilty person
decisions.reason: The verbs move from plural ("they", the man or woman of verse 6) to singular ("he"). Both refer to whoever committed the wrong.

decisions.choice: his guilt in its head: the payment for the wrong, the full original amount
decisions.reason: The word for guilt can name the guilt itself, the guilt offering, or, as here, the payment that makes up for the wrong. "In its head" means the principal, the whole sum taken (Leviticus 5:24). The ram offered to the LORD is mentioned separately in verse 8.

decisions.choice: its fifth: an extra twenty percent
decisions.reason: The wrongdoer pays back what was taken and a fifth more, as Leviticus 5:16, 24 requires.

decisions.choice: confess: say openly what one has done
decisions.reason: Leviticus 5:20-26 does not mention confession for this wrong, though Leviticus 5:5 requires it for other sins. Here the guilty person must name the sin as well as repay it.

decisions.choice: the guilty person
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies the subject at the change from "they" to "he", so that it is clear who repays. Readable keeps "they" throughout.

source.text: וְאִם־אֵ֨ין לָאִ֜ישׁ גֹּאֵ֗ל לְהָשִׁ֤יב הָאָשָׁם֙ אֵלָ֔יו הָאָשָׁ֛ם הַמּוּשָׁ֥ב לַיהוָ֖ה לַכֹּהֵ֑ן מִלְּבַ֗ד אֵ֚יל הַכִּפֻּרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְכַפֶּר־בּ֖וֹ עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And if there is not to the man a redeemer to return the guilt [payment] to him, the guilt [payment] returned [is] to Yahweh, for the priest, besides the ram of the atonements by which he makes atonement by it for him.

en.L: And if {{gender:the person|the man}} has no redeemer to whom the guilt [payment] may be repaid, the guilt [payment] that is repaid [belongs] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for the priest, besides the ram of atonement with which he makes atonement for him.
en.B: If the injured person has died and left no close relative to receive repayment, then what is repaid for the wrong goes to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which means to the priest. This is besides the ram of atonement, with which the priest makes atonement for the guilty one.
en.R: But the person who was wronged may have died and have no close relative to receive the payment. Then the payment belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and is given to the priest. The guilty person must also bring a ram so that the priest can make atonement for them.

decisions.choice: a redeemer: the nearest relative who acts on behalf of a family member
decisions.reason: The redeemer was the close relative who bought back family land or a relative sold into service, and who stood up for the family's rights (Leviticus 25:25, 48-49). Here he is the one who would receive the repayment in place of the person wronged.

decisions.choice: the man: the person who was wronged
decisions.reason: "The man" is the injured party. Since a living person would receive the payment himself, the case is one where that person has died and left no relative to receive it.

decisions.choice: to the LORD, for the priest: the payment goes to the sanctuary
decisions.reason: Wrong done to a neighbor is also wrong done to the LORD (verse 6). When no human can receive the payment, it goes to the LORD, which means it is given to the priest who serves him.

decisions.choice: the ram of atonement: the guilt offering ram
decisions.reason: The ram is the guilt offering of Leviticus 5:25, by which the priest makes atonement for the wrongdoer. It is offered whether or not the payment goes to a relative; the plural "atonements" names the purpose of the ram.

decisions.choice: has died / may have died
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state what the case implies, that the wronged person is no longer living. Literal leaves it implied.

decisions.choice: close relative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the redeemer is in this case, the relative who would receive the payment. Literal keeps "redeemer".

source.text: וְכָל־תְּרוּמָ֞ה לְכָל־קָדְשֵׁ֧י בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יַקְרִ֥יבוּ לַכֹּהֵ֖ן ל֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And every contribution of all [the] holy things of [the] sons of Israel which they bring to the priest, to him it shall be.

en.L: And every contribution among all the holy things of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, which they bring to the priest, shall be his.
en.B: Every contribution among all the holy gifts that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} bring to the priest will belong to him.
en.R: Every special gift among all the holy gifts that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} bring to a priest will belong to that priest.

decisions.choice: contribution: a portion set apart from a larger whole for holy use
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to lift or take off. It names a part set aside from goods or offerings and given to the LORD, and so to the priests (Exodus 25:2; Leviticus 7:14, 32).

decisions.choice: the holy things: gifts made holy by being given to the LORD
decisions.reason: These are offerings and gifts set apart for the sanctuary. Some of them were the priests' food and income (Leviticus 22:2-3; Numbers 18:8-19).

decisions.choice: special gift
decisions.reason: Readable uses "special gift" for the technical word "contribution", since the point is that the gift was set apart.

source.text: וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת־קֳדָשָׁ֖יו ל֣וֹ יִהְי֑וּ אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִתֵּ֥ן לַכֹּהֵ֖ן ל֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And [each] man, his holy things to him they shall be; [each] man who gives to the priest, to him it shall be.

en.L: And each one, his holy things shall be his; whatever each one gives to the priest, to him it shall be.'"
en.B: Each person's holy gifts are their own to give, but whatever anyone gives to a priest belongs to that priest.'"
en.R: The holy gifts people set apart are theirs to give as they choose. But whatever they give to a priest belongs to him.'"

decisions.choice: his holy things shall be his: the giver controls his gifts until they are given
alternatives: each priest keeps the holy things given to him
decisions.reason: The first "his" belongs to the giver. The second can refer to the giver, so that a person decides which priest receives the gift, or to the priest, so that each priest keeps the holy things given to him. The second half of the verse, "whatever anyone gives to the priest shall be his", fits the first reading: the gift is the giver's to give, and once given it belongs to that priest.

decisions.choice: their own to give / theirs to give as they choose
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the meaning decision; Literal keeps the open Hebrew wording.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: said to Moses
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

source.text: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ כִּֽי־תִשְׂטֶ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וּמָעֲלָ֥ה ב֖וֹ מָֽעַל׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel and say to them: [a] man, [a] man, when turns aside his wife and acts unfaithfully against him [an] unfaithfulness,

en.L: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'If any man's wife turns aside and acts unfaithfully against him,
en.B: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'Suppose a man's wife strays from him and breaks faith with him,
en.R: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Tell them: 'A man's wife may turn away from him and be unfaithful to him.

decisions.choice: a man, a man: any man at all
decisions.reason: Saying "man" twice makes the case general: whatever husband it may be (Leviticus 15:2; 17:3).

decisions.choice: turns aside: leaves the right way, here the faithfulness owed in marriage
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn off a road (Proverbs 4:15; 7:25). In this chapter it is used of a wife who leaves her husband for another man (verses 19, 20, 29).

decisions.choice: acts unfaithfully against him: breaks the trust of the marriage
decisions.reason: This is the same word for unfaithfulness used of wronging the LORD in verse 6. Marriage is a bond of trust, and adultery breaks it.

decisions.choice: when: the start of a long case that runs to verse 15
decisions.reason: Verses 12-14 set out the situation and verse 15 gives what is to be done. The sentence carries on through several verses.

decisions.choice: Suppose
decisions.reason: Balanced opens the long case with "Suppose" so that the reader can follow the conditions in verses 12-14 before the instruction in verse 15.

source.text: וְשָׁכַ֨ב אִ֣ישׁ אֹתָהּ֮ שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע֒ וְנֶעְלַם֙ מֵעֵינֵ֣י אִישָׁ֔הּ וְנִסְתְּרָ֖ה וְהִ֣יא נִטְמָ֑אָה וְעֵד֙ אֵ֣ין בָּ֔הּ וְהִ֖וא לֹ֥א נִתְפָּֽשָׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: and lies a man with her [a] lying of seed, and it is hidden from [the] eyes of her husband, and she is concealed, and she has defiled herself, and [a] witness there is not against her, and she was not caught,

en.L: and a man lies with her [with] a lying of seed, and it is hidden from her husband's eyes, and she is concealed, and she has defiled herself, and there is no witness against her, and she was not caught,
en.B: and another man sleeps with her, but it is hidden from her husband; she has defiled herself in secret, there is no witness against her, and she was not caught,
en.R: Another man sleeps with her, but her husband does not know about it. She has made herself unclean in secret. No one saw it, and she was not caught.

decisions.choice: lies with her a lying of seed: has sexual intercourse with her
decisions.reason: The phrase is a plain description of intercourse used in the laws (Leviticus 15:18; 18:20; 19:20). The man is someone other than her husband.

decisions.choice: she has defiled herself: adultery made her unclean
decisions.reason: Adultery is called defiling oneself (Leviticus 18:20). The uncleanness here is moral, not the kind removed by washing, and it is the question the rest of the chapter seeks to settle.

decisions.choice: no witness: there is no way to prove the charge
decisions.reason: The law did not allow anyone to be convicted on suspicion; a charge had to be confirmed by witnesses (Deuteronomy 17:6; 19:15). Adultery could carry the death penalty (Leviticus 20:10). With no witness, the case cannot go to a court, so it is put before the LORD.

decisions.choice: another man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "another man" and "sleeps with" to make clear that the man is not her husband and what the phrase means. Literal keeps the Hebrew wording.

source.text: וְעָבַ֨ר עָלָ֧יו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָ֛ה וְקִנֵּ֥א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ וְהִ֣וא נִטְמָ֑אָה אוֹ־עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֤יו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָה֙ וְקִנֵּ֣א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וְהִ֖יא לֹ֥א נִטְמָֽאָה׃

records.literal_gloss: and passes over him a spirit of jealousy and he is jealous of his wife, and she has defiled herself; or passes over him a spirit of jealousy and he is jealous of his wife, and she has not defiled herself,

en.L: and a spirit of jealousy passes over him and he is jealous of his wife, and she has defiled herself; or a spirit of jealousy passes over him and he is jealous of his wife, though she has not defiled herself,
en.B: and a fit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of his wife, and she has in fact defiled herself; or if a fit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of his wife though she has not defiled herself,
en.R: Then a strong feeling of jealousy comes over her husband, and he suspects her. Perhaps she has made herself unclean, or perhaps she has not, but he is still jealous and suspects her.

decisions.choice: a spirit of jealousy: a strong feeling of jealousy that takes hold of him
decisions.reason: "Spirit" here means a mood or passion that comes over a person, as in "a spirit of whoredom" (Hosea 4:12) or "a spirit of distress" (Isaiah 61:3). It is not a spirit being.

decisions.choice: jealous of his wife: suspicious of her faithfulness
decisions.reason: The verb describes the passion of someone who claims a relationship as his alone and fears it is betrayed (Proverbs 6:34). It is not envy. The same word is used of the LORD, who will not share his people with other gods (Exodus 20:5; 34:14).

decisions.choice: she has defiled herself, or she has not: the law covers both cases
decisions.reason: The husband's suspicion alone sets the procedure in motion, whether the wife is guilty or innocent. Only the LORD knows which is true, and the ritual leaves the answer to him (verses 27-28).

decisions.choice: a fit of jealousy
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "fit of jealousy" for "spirit of jealousy" to avoid the impression of a spirit being; Readable says "a strong feeling of jealousy". Literal keeps "spirit".

decisions.choice: but he is still jealous and suspects her
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the husband's suspicion after the second case, as the Hebrew does by repeating the whole clause.

source.text: וְהֵבִ֨יא הָאִ֣ישׁ אֶת־אִשְׁתּוֹ֮ אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן֒ וְהֵבִ֤יא אֶת־קָרְבָּנָהּ֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ עֲשִׂירִ֥ת הָאֵיפָ֖ה קֶ֣מַח שְׂעֹרִ֑ים לֹֽא־יִצֹ֨ק עָלָ֜יו שֶׁ֗מֶן וְלֹֽא־יִתֵּ֤ן עָלָיו֙ לְבֹנָ֔ה כִּֽי־מִנְחַ֤ת קְנָאֹת֙ ה֔וּא מִנְחַ֥ת זִכָּר֖וֹן מַזְכֶּ֥רֶת עָוֺֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: then shall bring the man his wife to the priest, and bring her offering for her, a tenth of the ephah of flour of barley; not he shall pour on it oil, and not put on it frankincense, for [a] grain offering of jealousies it [is], a grain offering of remembrance, bringing to remembrance iniquity.

en.L: then the man shall bring his wife to the priest, and he shall bring her offering for her, a tenth of an ephah of barley flour; he shall not pour oil on it nor put frankincense on it, for a grain offering of jealousies it [is], a grain offering of remembrance, which brings iniquity to mind.
en.B: the man is to bring his wife to the priest. He must also bring the offering required for her, {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of barley flour. He is not to pour oil on it or add frankincense, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance that calls guilt to mind.
en.R: The man must bring his wife to the priest. He must also bring an offering for her: {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of barley flour. He must not put any olive oil or incense on it. This is because it is a grain offering about jealousy. It is an offering that brings a hidden wrong to mind.

decisions.choice: barley flour, with no oil or frankincense: a plain offering, not a joyful one
decisions.reason: Ordinary grain offerings were of fine wheat flour with oil and frankincense (Leviticus 2:1). Barley was the cheaper grain. Like the sin offering of the poor (Leviticus 5:11), this offering has no oil or frankincense, because it is brought over a suspected wrong.

decisions.choice: a grain offering of jealousies: an offering brought because of jealousy
decisions.reason: The plural "jealousies" names the matter the offering concerns: the husband's jealousy and the question it raises (also verses 18, 25, 29).

decisions.choice: a grain offering of remembrance, bringing iniquity to remembrance: it puts the matter of guilt before the LORD
decisions.reason: The offering "reminds" in the sense of calling the case to the LORD's attention so that he may act on it. Elsewhere bringing iniquity to remembrance means exposing guilt that is there (1 Kings 17:18; Ezekiel 29:16). If there is no guilt, nothing is found (verse 28).

decisions.choice: her offering for her: brought by the husband on her behalf
decisions.reason: The husband provides the offering, but it is offered for the wife, since her case is the one to be decided.

decisions.choice: about 2 quarts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with "a tenth of an ephah" as the alternative. Literal keeps the Hebrew unit.

decisions.choice: incense / a hidden wrong
decisions.reason: Readable uses "incense" for frankincense, a sweet-smelling resin burned with offerings, and "a hidden wrong" for iniquity, since the case is one where any guilt is secret (verse 13).

source.text: וְהִקְרִ֥יב אֹתָ֖הּ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְהֶֽעֱמִדָ֖הּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall bring her near the priest and make her stand before Yahweh.

en.L: And the priest shall bring her near and make her stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The priest is to bring her near and set her in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The priest must bring her forward and have her stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: before the LORD: at the sanctuary, in his presence
decisions.reason: To stand before the LORD is to be brought to the sanctuary, in the courtyard near the altar (verse 25), where cases too hard for people were laid before him (Exodus 22:7-8).

decisions.choice: at the tabernacle
decisions.reason: Readable says where she stands "before the LORD", at the tabernacle. Literal and Balanced keep the phrase as it is.

source.text: וְלָקַ֧ח הַכֹּהֵ֛ן מַ֥יִם קְדֹשִׁ֖ים בִּכְלִי־חָ֑רֶשׂ וּמִן־הֶֽעָפָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִהְיֶה֙ בְּקַרְקַ֣ע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן יִקַּ֥ח הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְנָתַ֥ן אֶל־הַמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall take the priest holy water in a vessel of clay, and from the dust which is on [the] floor of the tabernacle shall take the priest and put into the water.

en.L: And the priest shall take holy water in a vessel of clay, and some of the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle the priest shall take and put into the water.
en.B: Then the priest is to put holy water in a clay pot, take some of the dust that lies on the tabernacle floor, and add it to the water.
en.R: Then the priest must pour some holy water into a jar made of clay. He must take some dust from the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.

decisions.choice: holy water: water set apart for use at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The phrase occurs only here. The water may be from the bronze basin at the tabernacle, where the priests washed (Exodus 30:18-21), but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: dust from the floor of the tabernacle: earth from the holy place itself
decisions.reason: The dust comes from the ground of the sanctuary, where the LORD dwells. The water the woman drinks is ordinary water mixed with dust and, later, ink (verse 23); its power comes from the LORD, not from what is in it (verse 21).

decisions.choice: an earthen vessel: a common clay pot
decisions.reason: Clay pots were the everyday containers of the time. The plain vessel suits the plain offering of verse 15.

source.text: וְהֶעֱמִ֨יד הַכֹּהֵ֥ן אֶֽת־הָאִשָּׁה֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֒ וּפָרַע֙ אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וְנָתַ֣ן עַל־כַּפֶּ֗יהָ אֵ֚ת מִנְחַ֣ת הַזִּכָּר֔וֹן מִנְחַ֥ת קְנָאֹ֖ת הִ֑וא וּבְיַ֤ד הַכֹּהֵן֙ יִהְי֔וּ מֵ֥י הַמָּרִ֖ים הַמְאָֽרֲרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall make stand the priest the woman before Yahweh, and let loose the head of the woman, and put on her palms the grain offering of the remembrance, [a] grain offering of jealousies it [is], and in [the] hand of the priest shall be the waters of the bitter [things] that bring the curse.

en.L: And the priest shall set the woman before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and loosen [the hair of] the woman's head, and put on her palms the grain offering of remembrance — it [is] the grain offering of jealousy — and in the priest's hand shall be the waters of bitterness that bring the curse.
en.B: The priest is to set the woman before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, let down her hair, and put the grain offering of remembrance, the grain offering for jealousy, into her hands. In his own hand the priest is to hold the bitter water that carries the curse.
en.R: The priest must have the woman stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He must loosen her hair and put the grain offering in her hands. It is the offering about jealousy that brings the matter to mind. The priest himself must hold the bitter water that carries the curse.

decisions.choice: let loose the head: let her hair hang loose, unbound
decisions.reason: The verb means to let go or let hang free. Of the head it means letting the hair down, or perhaps uncovering it, a sign of mourning or disgrace (Leviticus 10:6; 13:45; 21:10). Here it marks her as a woman under suspicion.

decisions.choice: the water of bitterness that brings the curse: water that causes bitter suffering if she is guilty
decisions.reason: "Bitterness" refers to the bitter pain the water brings on a guilty woman (verses 24, 27), and the second word means "bringing a curse", from the verb "to curse". The water is not said to taste bitter; its name describes what it does.

decisions.choice: she holds the offering, the priest holds the water
decisions.reason: The woman holds the offering that brings her case before the LORD, and the priest holds the water that will decide it, until the offering is presented (verses 25-26).

decisions.choice: the bitter water
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable shorten "the water of bitterness" to "the bitter water", the natural English form, here and through the chapter. Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

source.text: וְהִשְׁבִּ֨יעַ אֹתָ֜הּ הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְאָמַ֤ר אֶל־הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אִם־לֹ֨א שָׁכַ֥ב אִישׁ֙ אֹתָ֔ךְ וְאִם־לֹ֥א שָׂטִ֛ית טֻמְאָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת אִישֵׁ֑ךְ הִנָּקִ֕י מִמֵּ֛י הַמָּרִ֥ים הַֽמְאָרֲרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall make her swear the priest and say to the woman: if not has lain a man with you, and if not you have turned aside [to] uncleanness under your husband, be free from [the] waters of the bitter [things] that bring the curse, these.

en.L: And the priest shall make her swear and say to the woman, "If a man has not lain with you, and if you have not turned aside [into] uncleanness under your husband, be free from the waters of bitterness, these that bring the curse.
en.B: Then the priest is to put her under oath and say to her, "If no man but your husband has slept with you, and you have not turned aside to uncleanness while you are bound to him, you will be free from the harm of this bitter water that carries the curse.
en.R: Then the priest must make her take an oath. He must say to her, "If no other man has slept with you, and you have not been unfaithful to your husband and made yourself unclean, then this bitter water that carries the curse will not harm you.

decisions.choice: under your husband: while you are bound to your husband in marriage
decisions.reason: A wife was said to be "under" her husband, under his authority and in his household (Ezekiel 23:5). The phrase does not refer to anything before the marriage.

decisions.choice: be free: be unharmed, cleared of the charge
decisions.reason: The verb means to be free from guilt or punishment (Exodus 21:19; Numbers 5:28, 31). Spoken by the priest, it declares that the water will do the innocent woman no harm.

decisions.choice: if not ...: the oath is spoken as a condition
decisions.reason: The priest speaks the oath, and the woman takes it on herself by answering "Amen" (verse 22). The first half deals with an innocent woman, the second (verses 20-21) with a guilty one.

decisions.choice: no other man / no man but your husband
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "other", since the man meant is anyone except her husband (verse 20). Literal keeps "no man".

source.text: וְאַ֗תְּ כִּ֥י שָׂטִ֛ית תַּ֥חַת אִישֵׁ֖ךְ וְכִ֣י נִטְמֵ֑את וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אִ֥ישׁ בָּךְ֙ אֶת־שְׁכָבְתּ֔וֹ מִֽבַּלְעֲדֵ֖י אִישֵֽׁךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: But you, if you have turned aside under your husband, and if you have defiled yourself, and given [a] man in you his lying, apart from your husband —

en.L: But you, if you have turned aside under your husband, and if you have defiled yourself, and a man has had his lying with you, apart from your husband —"
en.B: But if you have turned aside while bound to your husband, if you have defiled yourself and someone besides your husband has slept with you —"
en.R: But you may have been unfaithful while you were married to your husband. You may have made yourself unclean by sleeping with a man other than your husband."

decisions.choice: but you, if ...: the sentence breaks off and resumes in verse 21
decisions.reason: The priest's words stop after the condition, and verse 21 tells how he puts her under the curse before giving its words. The Hebrew gives the condition here and the curse there.

decisions.choice: a man has given his lying in you: a man has had intercourse with you
decisions.reason: This is another plain legal expression for sexual intercourse (Leviticus 18:20, 23; 20:15).
Literal and Balanced end the verse with a dash to show that the sentence is broken off and taken up again in verse 21. Readable makes the condition its own sentences.

source.text: וְהִשְׁבִּ֨יעַ הַכֹּהֵ֥ן אֶֽת־הָֽאִשָּׁה֮ בִּשְׁבֻעַ֣ת הָאָלָה֒ וְאָמַ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ לָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה יִתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה אוֹתָ֛ךְ לְאָלָ֥ה וְלִשְׁבֻעָ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ עַמֵּ֑ךְ בְּתֵ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְרֵכֵךְ֙ נֹפֶ֔לֶת וְאֶת־בִּטְנֵ֖ךְ צָבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and shall make swear the priest the woman with [the] oath of the curse, and shall say the priest to the woman: may make Yahweh you as a curse and as an oath in [the] midst of your people, when makes Yahweh your thigh falling and your belly swollen;

en.L: then the priest shall make the woman swear with the oath of the curse, and the priest shall say to the woman, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make you a curse and an oath in the midst of your people, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} makes your thigh fall away and your belly swell;
en.B: then the priest is to make the woman swear the oath of the curse, and he is to say to her, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make you a byword in curses and oaths among your people, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} makes your thigh waste away and your belly swell.
en.R: Then the priest must make the woman take the oath of the curse. He must say to her, "If you are guilty, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make your name a curse that your people use when they swear oaths. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make your womb shrink and your belly swell.

decisions.choice: make you a curse and an oath: make you an example people name when they curse or swear
alternatives: make you accursed and sworn against
decisions.reason: To become "a curse" is to suffer so plainly that others use your name in their curses: "May the LORD make you like her." Jeremiah 29:22 gives such a curse, and Isaiah 65:15 speaks of a name left behind "for a curse".

decisions.choice: your thigh falling and your belly swelling: harm to her body that ends her ability to bear children
alternatives: a wasting disease of the body
miscarriage of a child conceived in adultery
decisions.reason: "Thigh" is a polite word for the reproductive organs; children are said to come "out of the thigh" of their father (Genesis 46:26; Exodus 1:5). What exactly is meant is not certain: it may be a miscarriage, a fallen womb, or the loss of fertility. Verse 28 sets against it the promise that an innocent woman will conceive, so the curse at least means she will be unable to have children.

decisions.choice: when the LORD makes: the outcome is the LORD's doing
decisions.reason: The priest does not claim that the water works by itself. It is the LORD who brings the curse, if it comes, because only he knows what happened in secret (verse 13).

decisions.choice: then the priest shall make the woman swear: the narration takes up the oath broken off in verse 20
decisions.reason: After the condition of verse 20, this verse first says that the priest puts her under the curse, then gives the curse in his own words.

decisions.choice: a byword in curses and oaths
decisions.reason: Balanced says "byword" to show that the woman's name, not she herself, becomes the curse people repeat. Literal keeps "a curse and an oath".

decisions.choice: your womb shrink
decisions.reason: Readable says "womb" for "thigh", following the meaning decision that the word refers to the organs of childbearing. Literal and Balanced keep "thigh".

decisions.choice: If you are guilty
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the condition of verse 20, which Literal and Balanced leave hanging before the curse.

source.text: וּ֠בָאוּ הַמַּ֨יִם הַמְאָרְרִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ בְּֽמֵעַ֔יִךְ לַצְבּ֥וֹת בֶּ֖טֶן וְלַנְפִּ֣ל יָרֵ֑ךְ וְאָמְרָ֥ה הָאִשָּׁ֖ה אָמֵ֥ן׀אָמֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: and shall go the waters that bring the curse, these, into your inward parts, to make swell [the] belly and to make fall [the] thigh. And shall say the woman: Amen, amen.

en.L: and may these waters that bring the curse go into your inward parts, to make [your] belly swell and [your] thigh fall away." And the woman shall say, "Amen, amen."
en.B: May this water that carries the curse go inside you, to make your belly swell and your thigh waste away." And the woman is to say, "Amen, amen."
en.R: May this water that carries the curse go into your body. May it make your belly swell and your womb shrink." Then the woman must say, "Amen, amen."

decisions.choice: and may this water go: the curse continues as a wish
decisions.reason: The verb form follows the wish of verse 21 ("may the LORD make you") and continues it. It could also be read as a statement of what the water will do, but either way it is part of the curse the woman accepts.

decisions.choice: Amen, amen: so be it
decisions.reason: "Amen" means "it is true" or "let it be so". By saying it the woman takes the oath and its curse on herself (Deuteronomy 27:15-26). Saying it twice makes the answer solemn (Nehemiah 8:6; Psalm 41:14).

decisions.choice: inward parts: the inside of the body
decisions.reason: The word means the inner organs, the belly or womb. The water goes into her body and takes effect there, as verse 21 describes.

decisions.choice: womb
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.

source.text: וְ֠כָתַב אֶת־הָאָלֹ֥ת הָאֵ֛לֶּה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בַּסֵּ֑פֶר וּמָחָ֖ה אֶל־מֵ֥י הַמָּרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall write these curses the priest on the scroll, and wipe [them] off into [the] waters of the bitter [things].

en.L: And the priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wipe [them] off into the waters of bitterness.
en.B: The priest is to write these curses in a scroll and then rinse the writing off into the bitter water.
en.R: Then the priest must write these curses on a scroll. He must wash the ink off into the bitter water.

decisions.choice: write on a scroll and wipe off into the water: the words of the curse go into the water she drinks
decisions.reason: Ink of the time could be washed off leather or papyrus. The curse spoken in verses 21-22 is written and then dissolved into the water, so that the woman literally takes in the words she has accepted.

decisions.choice: wipe off: blot out, erase
decisions.reason: The verb is used of wiping a dish clean (2 Kings 21:13) and of blotting a name out of a book (Exodus 32:32-33).

decisions.choice: the ink
decisions.reason: Readable says what is washed off, the ink of the written curses.

source.text: וְהִשְׁקָה֙ אֶת־הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אֶת־מֵ֥י הַמָּרִ֖ים הַמְאָֽרֲרִ֑ים וּבָ֥אוּ בָ֛הּ הַמַּ֥יִם הַֽמְאָרֲרִ֖ים לְמָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he shall make drink the woman [the] waters of the bitter [things] that bring the curse, and shall go into her the waters that bring the curse to bitter [things].

en.L: And he shall make the woman drink the waters of bitterness that bring the curse, and the waters that bring the curse shall go into her [to become] bitter.
en.B: He is to have the woman drink the bitter water that carries the curse, and this water will go into her and bring bitter pain.
en.R: He must have the woman drink the bitter water that carries the curse. The water will go into her body to cause bitter pain.

decisions.choice: he shall make the woman drink: told here in advance of the order in verses 25-26
alternatives: she drinks once here and again in verse 26
decisions.reason: Verse 26 says that the woman drinks after the grain offering is burned. This verse states the act first, as a summary, before the steps are set out in order. It does not describe a second drinking.

decisions.choice: to bitterness: to cause bitter suffering
decisions.reason: The water goes into her to become bitter, that is, to bring pain. Verse 27 makes clear that this happens only if she is guilty.

source.text: וְלָקַ֤ח הַכֹּהֵן֙ מִיַּ֣ד הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה אֵ֖ת מִנְחַ֣ת הַקְּנָאֹ֑ת וְהֵנִ֤יף אֶת־הַמִּנְחָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְהִקְרִ֥יב אֹתָ֖הּ אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall take the priest from [the] hand of the woman the grain offering of the jealousies, and wave the grain offering before Yahweh, and bring it near to the altar.

en.L: And the priest shall take from the hand of the woman the grain offering of jealousies, and wave the grain offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and bring it near to the altar.
en.B: From the woman's hand the priest is to take the grain offering for jealousy. He is to wave the offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and present it at the altar.
en.R: The priest must take the grain offering about jealousy from the woman's hand. He must lift it up before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a gift to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and then bring it to the altar.

decisions.choice: wave: raise or move the offering before the LORD to present it to him
decisions.reason: Waving was a gesture of handing a gift over to the LORD before part of it went to the altar or to the priest (Leviticus 7:30; 8:27; 23:11).

decisions.choice: bring it near to the altar: present it at the altar
decisions.reason: A grain offering was brought to the altar before the priest burned a handful of it (Leviticus 2:8-9). The next verse gives that step.

decisions.choice: lift it up ... as a gift to him
decisions.reason: Readable explains the waving by what it meant, offering the gift to the LORD.

source.text: וְקָמַ֨ץ הַכֹּהֵ֤ן מִן־הַמִּנְחָה֙ אֶת־אַזְכָּ֣רָתָ֔הּ וְהִקְטִ֖יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה וְאַחַ֛ר יַשְׁקֶ֥ה אֶת־הָאִשָּׁ֖ה אֶת־הַמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall take a handful the priest from the grain offering, its memorial portion, and make [it] smoke on the altar, and after he shall make drink the woman the waters.

en.L: And the priest shall take a handful from the grain offering, its memorial portion, and make [it] go up in smoke on the altar, and after [that] he shall make the woman drink the waters.
en.B: Then the priest is to scoop up a handful of the grain offering, its memorial portion, and burn it on the altar, and only then make the woman drink the water.
en.R: Then the priest must take a handful of the grain offering. This is the part that is burned as a reminder. He must burn it on the altar. After that, he must have the woman drink the water.

decisions.choice: its memorial portion: the handful burned on the altar for the LORD
decisions.reason: The memorial portion is the part of a grain offering burned on the altar, while the rest went to the priests (Leviticus 2:2, 9; 5:12). The word is related to "remembrance" in verses 15 and 18: the offering brings the case before the LORD.

decisions.choice: make smoke: burn so that the smoke goes up
decisions.reason: The verb describes burning an offering on the altar, turning it into smoke that rises to the LORD (Leviticus 1:9; 2:2).

decisions.choice: afterward: the woman drinks once the offering has been made
decisions.reason: This sets the order of the ritual: the offering first, then the water (compare verse 24).

source.text: וְהִשְׁקָ֣הּ אֶת־הַמַּ֗יִם וְהָיְתָ֣ה אִֽם־נִטְמְאָה֮ וַתִּמְעֹ֣ל מַ֣עַל בְּאִישָׁהּ֒ וּבָ֨אוּ בָ֜הּ הַמַּ֤יִם הַמְאָֽרֲרִים֙ לְמָרִ֔ים וְצָבְתָ֣ה בִטְנָ֔הּ וְנָפְלָ֖ה יְרֵכָ֑הּ וְהָיְתָ֧ה הָאִשָּׁ֛ה לְאָלָ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב עַמָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he shall make her drink the waters, and it shall be, if she has defiled herself and acted unfaithfully [an] unfaithfulness against her husband, and shall go into her the waters that bring the curse to bitter [things], and shall swell her belly and fall her thigh, and shall become the woman a curse in [the] midst of her people.

en.L: And he shall make her drink the waters, and it shall be, if she has defiled herself and acted unfaithfully against her husband, that the waters that bring the curse shall go into her [to become] bitter, and her belly shall swell and her thigh shall fall away, and the woman shall become a curse in the midst of her people.
en.B: Once she has drunk the water, if she has in fact defiled herself and broken faith with her husband, the water that carries the curse will go into her and bring bitter pain. Her belly will swell, her thigh will waste away, and her name will become a curse among her people.
en.R: After she drinks the water, this is what will happen if she has made herself unclean and been unfaithful to her husband. The water that carries the curse will go into her and cause bitter pain. Her belly will swell and her womb will shrink. Her people will use her name when they curse someone.

decisions.choice: if she has defiled herself: the LORD makes the hidden truth known
decisions.reason: The case could not be settled by witnesses (verse 13). Water, dust and ink have no power of their own; the result shows the LORD's judgment (verse 21), and it falls only on a guilty woman.

decisions.choice: her belly shall swell and her thigh shall fall away
decisions.reason: As in verse 21: harm to the body that leaves her unable to bear children.

decisions.choice: become a curse: her name is used in curses
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.

decisions.choice: womb
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.

source.text: וְאִם־לֹ֤א נִטְמְאָה֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּטְהֹרָ֖ה הִ֑וא וְנִקְּתָ֖ה וְנִזְרְעָ֥ה זָֽרַע׃

records.literal_gloss: And if not has defiled herself the woman, and clean she [is], then she shall be free and shall be sown [with] seed.

en.L: And if the woman has not defiled herself, but clean she [is], then she shall be free and shall be sown [with] seed.
en.B: But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be cleared, and she will conceive children.
en.R: But if the woman has not made herself unclean and is clean, she will not be harmed. She will be able to have children.

decisions.choice: she shall be free: unharmed and cleared
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 19. The water does her no harm, and the suspicion against her is answered.

decisions.choice: be sown with seed: conceive and bear children
alternatives: she will be blessed with children
decisions.reason: The phrase means to conceive (Leviticus 12:2). It is the opposite of the curse of verses 21 and 27: the innocent woman keeps her ability to bear children. It may also promise that she will have them.

decisions.choice: clean: free of the uncleanness of adultery
decisions.reason: "Clean" answers "defiled herself" in this verse and in verses 13-14. It is the same pair of words used for ritual purity throughout the law.

decisions.choice: cleared
decisions.reason: Balanced says "cleared" to show that she is free of the suspicion; Readable says "will not be harmed", as in verse 19.

source.text: זֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַקְּנָאֹ֑ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּשְׂטֶ֥ה אִשָּׁ֛ה תַּ֥חַת אִישָׁ֖הּ וְנִטְמָֽאָה׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is the] law of the jealousies, when turns aside a wife under her husband and defiles herself,

en.L: This [is] the law of jealousies, when a wife turns aside under her husband and defiles herself,
en.B: This is the law for cases of jealousy, when a wife who is bound to her husband turns aside and defiles herself,
en.R: This is the law about jealousy. It is for a wife who is unfaithful to her husband and makes herself unclean.

decisions.choice: law: the set procedure for a case
decisions.reason: The word means instruction or teaching. Here, as in the closing lines of the laws in Leviticus (Leviticus 6:2; 7:1, 37; 11:46), it names the procedure to follow in a particular kind of case.

decisions.choice: when ...: the summary names the two cases of the law
decisions.reason: The closing summary repeats the two situations: a wife who has in fact been unfaithful (verse 29) and a husband who is jealous, whether or not she has (verse 30), as in verse 14.

source.text: א֣וֹ אִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תַּעֲבֹ֥ר עָלָ֛יו ר֥וּחַ קִנְאָ֖ה וְקִנֵּ֣א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְהֶעֱמִ֤יד אֶת־הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְעָ֤שָׂה לָהּ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַתּוֹרָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: or [a] man that passes over him a spirit of jealousy and he is jealous of his wife; and he shall make stand the woman before Yahweh, and shall do to her the priest all the law, this.

en.L: or a man over whom a spirit of jealousy passes, and he is jealous of his wife; and he shall make the woman stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the priest shall do to her all this law.
en.B: or when a fit of jealousy comes over a man and he becomes jealous of his wife. He is to have the woman stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the priest is to do for her everything this law requires.
en.R: It is also for a husband who becomes jealous and suspects his wife. He must have her stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the priest must do everything this law says.

decisions.choice: he shall make the woman stand: the husband brings her before the LORD
decisions.reason: The subject is the husband, who brings his wife to the priest (verse 15); the priest then sets her before the LORD (verses 16, 18). Both take part in bringing her into the LORD's presence.

decisions.choice: do to her all this law: carry out the whole procedure
decisions.reason: The priest follows every step of the ritual described in verses 15-28, so that the case is decided by the LORD and not by the husband.

decisions.choice: a fit of jealousy / becomes jealous
decisions.reason: As in verse 14.

source.text: וְנִקָּ֥ה הָאִ֖ישׁ מֵעָוֺ֑ן וְהָאִשָּׁ֣ה הַהִ֔וא תִּשָּׂ֖א אֶת־עֲוֺנָֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And shall be free the man from iniquity, and the woman, that [one], shall bear her iniquity.

en.L: And the man shall be clear of iniquity, and that woman shall bear her iniquity.'"
en.B: The husband will be clear of guilt, but the woman herself must bear her guilt.'"
en.R: The husband will not be guilty of any wrong. But if the woman is guilty, she must suffer the result of her sin.'"

decisions.choice: the man shall be free from iniquity: he bears no guilt for bringing the case
alternatives: he is cleared of guilt for having tolerated adultery in his house
decisions.reason: By following this law the husband is cleared of guilt, whatever the outcome: he has not wronged his wife by bringing his suspicion before the LORD, and he does not share her guilt if she has sinned.

decisions.choice: bear her iniquity: suffer the consequences of her own sin
decisions.reason: To bear one's iniquity is to carry its punishment (Leviticus 5:1; 20:17). The consequence falls on her alone, and only if she is guilty (verses 27-28).

decisions.choice: if the woman is guilty
decisions.reason: Readable states the condition the chapter has set out, so that the verse is not read as saying that every woman brought to the priest is guilty.
